stem: An adult has jaundice and an elevated total bilirubin level. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: Hyperbilirubinemia can result from increased bilirubin production, impaired hepatic handling or excretion, or biliary obstruction, so the result requires clinical correlation.
options.B: An elevated total bilirubin level in an adult is generally a benign normal variant and does not require consideration of hemolysis, liver disease, or obstruction.
options.C: Hyperbilirubinemia is primarily a neonatal finding, so an elevated adult bilirubin level has little meaningful differential diagnosis or clinical significance.
options.D: A total bilirubin elevation identifies one specific liver disease and can determine the cause of jaundice without bilirubin fractions or additional evaluation.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories guidance states that jaundice and bilirubinemia can result from disturbances in bilirubin production, uptake, storage, metabolism, and excretion. Mayo classifies causes as increased production such as hemolysis, decreased excretion such as obstruction or hepatitis, and abnormal metabolism. Therefore an elevated total bilirubin is not specific to one diagnosis and must be interpreted in clinical context, often with bilirubin fractions and other findings. A is correct.
educational_objective: Interpret elevated total bilirubin as a nonspecific finding arising from multiple production, hepatic-handling, metabolic, and excretory mechanisms.
source_version_date: Current Mayo test catalog; test-definition document generated May 19, 2026; live page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Useful For: evaluation of diseases affecting bilirubin production, uptake, storage, metabolism, or excretion. Clinical Information: jaundice may result from increased bilirubin production (eg, hemolysis), decreased excretion (eg, obstruction and hepatitis), or abnormal metabolism.
source_claim_supported: Adult hyperbilirubinemia has multiple possible mechanisms and total bilirubin alone does not identify one specific diagnosis.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor and interpret diagnostic/laboratory findings.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths and made each alternative a parallel interpretation of adult hyperbilirubinemia.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — Mayo directly lists multiple mechanisms of jaundice/hyperbilirubinemia; A uniquely preserves the nonspecific interpretation.
